title: Workers and students march in Rennes over cost of living and social policies
seoTitle: Rennes march against cost of living

tea.why: Protesters marched to express dissatisfaction with the cost of living, wages, pensions, and conditions in hospitals and education.
tea.want: Participants demanded government action on salaries, retirement benefits, and public services.
tea.changed: Nov 5: The protest concluded in the evening following clashes between demonstrators and police in the city center.

summary: On November 5, 2026, a large-scale demonstration took place in Rennes, France, as workers, students, and retirees marched to protest the rising cost of living and demand improvements to wages, pensions, and public services. Organised by an inter-union coalition, the march began at Place de Bretagne. Estimates of the crowd size varied, with the prefecture reporting at least 20,600 participants, while unions claimed up to 35,000. The event was marked by clashes between police and groups of masked individuals, particularly on Avenue Janvier and Place de Bretagne. Authorities reported property damage, including the ransacking of a hotel, and the use of tear gas and water cannons by police. Several individuals were injured, and the prefecture confirmed multiple arrests related to the property damage and confrontations.
response: The Ille-et-Vilaine prefecture stated that security forces intervened to address property damage and projectile throwing, leading to the arrest of several dozen individuals. Police deployed water cannons, armored vehicles, and tear gas during the clashes.

crowd.text: Between 20,600 and 35,000 people according to prefecture and union estimates.

arrests.text: Several dozen individuals were arrested according to the prefecture.

injuries.text: Five people required medical assistance, and at least three protesters were injured.

updates.text: The march began in the afternoon following authorization from the prefecture.
Clashes occurred on Avenue Janvier, leading to property damage at a local hotel.
Police used tear gas and water cannons on Place de Bretagne as tensions escalated.
The protest ended in the evening after police dispersed remaining groups on the esplanade de Gaulle.
